content.title: Pensacola's Keyla Richardson advances again, makes 'American Idol' Top 14
content.text: Updated March 30, 2026, 7:24 p.m. CTPensacola native Keyla Richardson has advanced to the Top 14 on "American Idol" following the show's first round of live votingRichardson's son, Drew, has been a major motivator for her throughout her journey on the showHer musical career began with singing gospel in Pensacola churches, and she has previously appeared on BET's "Sunday Best"Richardson's performance of "With A Little Help From My Friends" was highly praised by judge Lionel RichiePensacola’s own Keyla Richardson is now part of the "American Idol" Top 14 after successfully passing through the show's first round of live voting, in which America decided her fate on the show.Last week, Richardson's unique rendition of the Beatles' "With A Little Help From My Friends" left a strong impression on the music industry, establishing Richardson as a show frontrunner. Celebrity judge Lionel Richie credited the performance as one of the best he has heard on the show.As it turns out, the performance pleased viewers as well, who voted her into the Top 14.How do I vote on 'American Idol'With the 14 singers chosen for the next round, voting has opened.Longtime "Idol" viewers should know that the show got rid of its app, so voting is now available only through the website, over text and via social media comments. You can vote up to 10 times per contestant per platform until the last commercial break in tonight's episode.Voters will still be able to vote the traditional way online at AmericanIdol.com/Vote and over text. For text message voting, text the number of the finalist you would like to vote for to “21523”. For text message voting, text the number of the finalist you would like to vote for to “21523.” Richardson’s voting number is 20.From now on, each week’s voters will decide who moves forward until one contestant is ultimately crowned the next “American Idol.”The American Idol Season 24 finale is scheduled for May 18.Richardson advances through Hawaii performances, stops by PensacolaRichardson successfully passed through the show’s new Ohana Round at Disney’s Aulani Resort in Hawaii, securing her space in the Top 20. The remaining contestants performed again in Hawaii, this time for America's votes rather than the judges'. Their performances aired in two parts, on March 16 and March 23, as pre-recorded episodes. While Richardson's performance did not air until March 23, Richardson attended a watch party for the March 16 episode at Andy D’s on Pensacola Bay with her 9-year-old son, Drew, where she was surrounded by family, friends and fans cheering her on in her American Idol journey.For Richardson, seeing the Pensacola community support her throughout her journey has had her "getting teary-eyed" throughout the season.“Just having a supportive hometown means a lot. … Just seeing them support something positive, it’s everything to me. It really touches my heart," Richardson told the News Journal. "I’ve been getting teary-eyed all the time because that’s all I want to bring, some positive energy and just shed some light.”Keyla Richardson’s road to the Top 20Richardson received her coveted golden ticket on "American Idol" after an emotional audition on the Season 24 premiere on Jan. 26, even bringing Bryan to tears with her soulful rendition of “Glitter in the Air” by P!nk. After three unanimous “yes” votes, the judges gave her the green light, clearing her way to Hollywood week.“The audition process, it was a lot. It was very tedious. I was a nervous wreck,” Richardson told the News Journal. “My mind was everywhere. I was just ready to audition…you have to wait around, so many people ahead of you. Early mornings, it was a lot. I pushed through because this is what I wanted to do, and I wanted it to work out.”Since Richardson’s audition was aired in episode one, Richardson wasn’t on-screen again until the start of Hollywood Week on Feb. 23, nearly a month after her debut.There, Richardson continued to wow the judges, earning a standing ovation from her rendition of “I Won’t Give Up” by Jason Mraz.Richardson’s performance earned her temporary safety in the “American Idol” Golden Room, exempting her from an initial round of cuts from the judges.Richardson’s son, Drew, is a major motivator for RichardsonRichardson’s son, Drew, has been a major part of her "American Idol' journey, often captured on camera mouthing the words to her songs during performances and even sitting in Underwood’s judging chair during Hollywood Week.Richardson credits Drew with motivating her to be on the show."My performance tonight is for my son Drew," Richardson shared on social media on March 9. "Today, tomorrow, and for all the years to come."The judges also shared tender moments with Drew, particularly during Richardson’s initial audition.During Richardson's audition, Drew was even able to "audition" himself, singing "God Only Knows" before the panel of judges. The moment that captured America's heart was also a point of pride for Richardson.“Seeing my son interact with the judges, just him being a natural in front of the camera. But when he got on camera, it blew my mind. So those reactions you got, those were the real reactions,” Richardson said. “I’ve never seen him talk in such a way and do things in such a way. It was almost like a superpower. Like God just did something, and you were surprised…I’m so happy to know that I think my baby has a gift.”Richardson’s musical journey started in PensacolaRichardson has been singing almost her entire life, starting with singing gospel in Pensacola's churches.“I’ve always had a love for singing. I’ve been singing since the age of 5. I was raised in the church and so I just wanted to do more,” Richardson said. “I felt like I was just in a box and I just wanted to branch out and see what they got in store for me.”She went on to become a music teacher at Life Shifting Learning Academy on Pensacola Boulevard, where she’s been for about six years. She knows what it’s like to need someone to believe in you, and also importantly, to learn to believe in yourself. Now, she works to help young people develop their voices and gets to be the one who believes in them.Now, when Richardson visits her students during the season, she is able to pass along lots of hugs and a few words of wisdom.“They hug on me, love on me. I have to make them do their work,” Richardson said of her students. “I just want to let the world know, never give up. Always chase your dream, don’t let nobody stop you chasing your dream. You just keep going, no matter what.”Has Richardson been on TV before?Richardson has showcased her voice on television before. She landed in the top four of BET’s “Sunday Best,” which allows aspiring gospel artists to learn from the artists they grew up listening to, to meet peers, and share their talent with a vast new audience.Opportunities only continued to open from there, leading her to claim her first No. 1 on Billboard’s Gospel Airplay for her single “So Good.” She would go on to earn the role of Vicky Waters in the 2022 film “Due Season,” starring alongside actress Vivica A. Fox.However, auditioning for 'American Idol' had long been a dream of hers, and she felt it was time to pursue it. Now, she wants to motivate others to do the same.“The most I’ve taken out of it is just to keep going, even when you don’t feel like it, even if you don’t feel like you can’t do it – you can do it. Anything you put your mind to, I say it all the time, but that’s the thing I took out of it just to keep pushing," Richardson said.How to watch season 24 of 'American Idol'ABC airs "American Idol" at 7 p.m. CDT every Monday. If you don't have cable, paid streaming platforms also show episodes in real time, such as YouTube TV, DirecTV, Fubo, Sling, Hulu + Live TV and more. If you missed it, the episode is then available to stream on Hulu the next day.
